pr.title: coverage: Clean up marker statements that aren't needed later
pr.description:
Some of the marker statements used by coverage are added during MIR building for use by the InstrumentCoverage pass (during analysis), and are not needed afterwards.

@rustbot label +A-code-coverage
pr.author: Zalathar

processing.reason: The PR changes only compiler-internal coverage marker statements: CleanupPostBorrowck turns `StatementKind::Coverage(BlockMarker/SpanMarker)` into `nop` after InstrumentCoverage has consumed them, while retaining CounterIncrement/ExpressionUsed. Before the PR those marker statements survived and were explicitly ignored by codegen (`CoverageKind::SpanMarker | CoverageKind::BlockMarker { .. } => return`), and validation accepted all Coverage statements after analysis. Marker statements are no-ops during codegen, so retaining them versus erasing them cannot change any runtime value, control flow, character, or boolean. The accompanying test `tests/mir-opt/instrument_coverage_cleanup.rs` asserts only MIR structure (`EMIT_MIR` diffs and CHECK-NOT/CHECK on statement kinds); it makes no execution or value assertion. Consequently no source-grounded pair of same-signature Rust functions can model this rewrite as a defined-execution value difference: the original (markers retained) and transformed (markers nop'd) implementations must always agree when executed. Producing a differing pair would require adding an arbitrary, PR-unjustified return-value change, which the task forbids. This is an optimization/internal-representation cleanup, not a miscompilation with observable semantics.

analysis.summary: CleanupPostBorrowck now erases coverage marker statements (SpanMarker and BlockMarker) that MIR building inserted for InstrumentCoverage's analysis, after InstrumentCoverage has consumed them. Coverage statements added by InstrumentCoverage itself (CounterIncrement, ExpressionUsed) must remain. Validation in the PostCleanup phase and codegen both now assume marker statements are gone, so cleanup must be selective rather than deleting all StatementKind::Coverage.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, coverage marker statements survived beyond analysis: codegen explicitly early-returned for them, and the MIR validator did not reject them after analysis. The patch description states: "Some of the marker statements used by coverage are added during MIR building for use by the InstrumentCoverage pass (during analysis), and are not needed afterwards." The old codegen branch was: "CoverageKind::SpanMarker | CoverageKind::BlockMarker { .. } => return," with the comment "Marker statements have no effect during codegen, so return early and don't create `func_coverage`." The old validator grouped all Coverage statements into the allowed no-op arm.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically wrong state is that SpanMarker/BlockMarker statements remain in MIR after InstrumentCoverage and are merely tolerated downstream by an early return in codegen and by validation that accepts all Coverage statements after analysis. This PR replaces that with CleanupPostBorrowck turning exactly BlockMarker/SpanMarker into nop statements after InstrumentCoverage, while leaving CounterIncrement and ExpressionUsed intact. A related incorrect rewrite to guard against would be deleting all StatementKind::Coverage (including InstrumentCoverage-added CounterIncrement/ExpressionUsed), but the actual historical behavior described by this patch is marker retention/tolerance, not wholesale coverage deletion.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR of Rust functions compiled with coverage instrumentation enabled, especially branch coverage, observed between MIR building, the InstrumentCoverage analysis pass, and CleanupPostBorrowck. Relevant statements are StatementKind::Coverage with CoverageKind::SpanMarker, BlockMarker { id }, CounterIncrement { id }, and ExpressionUsed { id }. The regression test uses `-Cinstrument-coverage -Zcoverage-options=branch -Zno-profiler-runtime` and a branch such as `if !core::hint::black_box(true) {}`.
analysis.trigger: Running CleanupPostBorrowck on MIR that contains coverage marker statements inserted during MIR building, after InstrumentCoverage has already used those markers to build branch/counter/expression coverage mappings.
preconditions: Coverage instrumentation is enabled for the function (e.g. -Cinstrument-coverage).
InstrumentCoverage has already run and consumed the MIR-building marker statements.
CleanupPostBorrowck runs after InstrumentCoverage in the pass pipeline and turns BlockMarker/SpanMarker into nop.
Validation at MirPhase::Analysis(AnalysisPhase::PostCleanup) or later requires marker statements to be absent.
CounterIncrement and ExpressionUsed statements added by InstrumentCoverage must not be removed by this cleanup.
pitfalls: Removing all StatementKind::Coverage statements, which would also delete CounterIncrement and ExpressionUsed that are needed for codegen coverage counters/expressions.
Removing BlockMarker/SpanMarker too early, i.e. before InstrumentCoverage analysis has consumed them for branch mapping.
Assuming the old codegen early return is sufficient: the pass now enforces that markers are gone before codegen.
Treating a retained test name or old comment as proof that a replacement pass is incorrect; compare actual before/after MIR assignments.
Conflating marker cleanup with unrelated borrow/copy transformations handled by the same pass.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a mir-opt test that emits MIR for both InstrumentCoverage and CleanupPostBorrowck using `-Cinstrument-coverage -Zcoverage-options=branch -Zno-profiler-runtime` plus `--remap-path-prefix`. The test should assert that after CleanupPostBorrowck no `Coverage::BlockMarker` or `Coverage::SpanMarker` remains, while `Coverage::CounterIncrement` (and ExpressionUsed) are retained. Compare the two diffs: InstrumentCoverage adds CounterIncrement/ExpressionUsed and leaves markers in place; CleanupPostBorrowck changes only the markers to `nop` and leaves counters/expressions untouched. Do not claim execution; these are compiler-emitted MIR expectations.
evidence: Some of the marker statements used by coverage are added during MIR building
for use by the InstrumentCoverage pass (during analysis), and are not needed afterwards.
